problem.title: Lighting fails between the trades.
problem.body: On most construction projects, lighting is split across separate vendors. An architect or interior designer selects the concept, an electrical engineer calculates the power loads, a supplier sells the fixtures, and a contractor installs the wiring. No single team owns the whole sequence.

meta.title: Studio — CROIX
meta.description: CROIX Lighting Design Studio — Milanese design leadership and Manila engineering for architectural lighting, photometric verification, and control systems.

hero.title: A practice built around light.
hero.intro: CROIX is a turnkey lighting design and engineering studio. Milanese design leadership, Manila technical delivery, and one accountable team from first sketch to opening night.

who.title: The last five percent.
who.lead: You can spend months planning a building and sourcing stone, timber, and fabrics. The final appearance and comfort of that space still depend on how it is lit.
paragraphs: Lighting determines how a room functions and looks the moment someone walks through the door. It is the difference between a hotel lobby that feels welcome, an office where people can work all day without eye strain, and a building exterior that remains safe and visible at night.

CROIX, together with our Italian sister studio LUMEA Collective, provides complete turnkey lighting and control solutions from initial concept to final installation. We combine architectural lighting design from Milan with illumination and control systems engineering in Metro Manila.

We partner with property developers, architects, interior designers, electrical contractors, engineers, and lighting suppliers around the world. Indoor light should be as comfortable as natural daylight; outdoor light should guide people safely without wasting electricity or polluting the night sky.
who.imageAlt: Daylight falling through a quiet concrete stair

mission.label: Mission
mission.title: Comfortable inside. Safe outside. On time and on budget.
mission.body: To deliver complete turnkey lighting design, photometric engineering, and control system solutions that make indoor spaces comfortable for occupants, keep outdoor environments safe from glare and light pollution, and help construction teams complete projects on time and within budget.

vision.label: Vision
vision.title: The trusted lighting partner across borders.
vision.body: To be the trusted global lighting and engineering partner for property developers, architects, contractors, and lighting suppliers, setting the practical standard for built environments where architectural materials, electrical systems, and human visual comfort work together reliably.

timeline.title: Light, nature, and the spaces we share.
timeline.intro: The studio grew out of visualisation, luminaire manufacturing, field research, and a Milan–Manila partnership. The through-line is the same: light has to work for the people in the room and for the sky outside it.

items.label: 01 / Visualisation
items.title: Rooms that only worked when the light was right
items.body: While studying architecture at the University of Santo Tomas, Jonathan “Balong” Dela Cruz spent thousands of hours producing commissioned 3D architectural visualisations. High-end furniture and textured finishes only succeeded when the lighting was accurately placed — the observation that led him to specialise in illumination design.

items.label: 02 / Light Plan
items.title: A studio apprenticeship, and a shared standard
items.body: After working with several architecture firms, Jonathan joined Light Plan, Inc., a pioneering lighting design studio at the time, and invited his former colleague Charmaine “Ming” Javier-Fornarelli to the studio. Together they contributed to the 2011 and 2016 Philippine Lighting Conferences.

items.label: 03 / Manufacturing
items.title: Learning how fixtures are actually built
items.body: Jonathan moved into luminaire production and lamp distribution to understand how fixtures are engineered, sourced, and installed. That experience now informs the studio’s optical reviews, value engineering, and independent procurement policy.

items.label: 04 / Field research
items.title: The cost of over-lighting
items.body: As early LED technology spread, lower electricity consumption led owners to over-light spaces with harsh, glaring fixtures. Jonathan documented the effects — indoor eye strain and outdoor light pollution — across the Sierra Madre mountains, the firefly habitats of Iwahig in Palawan, and pawikan conservation sites in La Union with CURMA. During the COVID-19 pandemic, he also documented how poorly specified household LEDs caused daily eye fatigue, headaches, and migraines.

items.label: 05 / Milan
items.title: European design leadership
items.body: Charmaine became a licensed architect, practised with C.T. Onglao Architects and developer VConsunji, then moved to Italy to earn her Master’s Degree in Lighting Design and LED Technology at Politecnico di Milano. She practised in Milan with studios including Voltaire Light Design before founding LUMEA Collective.

items.label: 06 / One practice
items.title: Milan and Manila, in the same drawing set
items.body: As LUMEA’s European practice grew, Charmaine needed a dedicated engineering team in the Philippines. Jonathan was building CROIX in Metro Manila around the same time. The two practices now operate as one delivery team: Milanese design direction, Manila engineering, and on-site commissioning across time zones.

model.intro: One practice, two centres of gravity. The design direction sits close to the European architecture and hospitality market; the engineering hub sits close to the drawings, contractors, and site conditions where the work is built.

cards.label: Milan / LUMEA Collective

A Politecnico di Milano graduate and licensed architect, she sets the creative and technical standard across heritage landmarks, corporate headquarters, and luxury hospitality — often alongside European studios including Voltaire Light Design, In-visible lab, and Sergio Boccia Lighting Design.
points: Concept, daylighting, and atmosphere
Heritage and hospitality design review

cards.body: The Metro Manila hub turns the design into buildable documentation: DIALux evo verification, AutoCAD and Revit layouts, control architecture, load schedules, procurement support, and on-site commissioning. Electrical engineers trained in government plan review close the loop between design intent and inspection.
points: Photometrics and false-colour verification
RCP, SLD, cable schedules, load computations
Controls integration and programming
Nighttime aiming, lux verification, handover

principles.title: How we make decisions.
principles.intro: These are the constraints we bring to every project — before the fixture schedule, before the renders, and before the budget conversation.

items.title: Human comfort first
items.body: Glare, colour rendering, and vertical illuminance are treated as design constraints, not finishing touches. A room should feel comfortable after an hour, not just photogenic for a minute.

items.title: Protect the night sky
items.body: Outdoor light is shielded, aimed, and dimmed so it lands on people and surfaces rather than drifting upward. DarkSky principles are part of the brief, not an afterthought.

items.title: Stay brand-neutral
items.body: CROIX does not manufacture or sell fixtures. Schedules, Bills of Quantities, and value-engineering reviews are written without a product allegiance — so the specification is defensible.

items.title: Prove it
items.body: DIALux evo calculations, false-colour illuminance maps, UGR reports, load schedules, and code paths leave the studio with the design. The numbers are part of the deliverable.

hero.title: The people behind your project.
hero.intro: Creative leadership in Europe and deep engineering capability in Asia — giving your project well-rounded support across every time zone.

bench.label: The bench
bench.intro: CROIX is deliberately small at the top and deep in the middle. The people who win the project are the people who draw it, calculate it, specify it, and stand on site at commissioning. Partner specialists are named as partners, not folded into the studio.

members.name: Jonathan “Balong” Dela Cruz
bio: Jonathan establishes the corporate strategy, international partnerships, global supplier networks, and business operations of CROIX. Trained in business since childhood and educated in architecture at the University of Santo Tomas, he brings executive experience in luminaire manufacturing, lamp distribution, and optical engineering.

From the primary engineering hub in Metro Manila, he governs turnkey project delivery and studio production for property developers, architects, and contractors worldwide. Because the studio operates independently of fixture manufacturers, he enforces unbiased procurement policies, value-engineering standards, and equipment budget controls across every engagement.

Outside the studio, he is an active member of the Philippine Native Tree Enthusiasts (PNTE), studying, conserving, and promoting native trees across the Philippines. His conservation research in forest and coastal ecosystems guides CROIX’s commitment to human visual comfort and the protection of the nocturnal environment.

members.name: Ar. Charmaine “Ming” Javier-Fornarelli
bio: Charmaine directs the global design division from Milan, serving as Principal Lighting Designer of CROIX and Founder of its Italian sister practice, LUMEA Collective. A licensed architect with a Master’s Degree in Lighting Design and LED Technology from Politecnico di Milano, she sets the studio’s creative and technical standards across historic landmarks, corporate headquarters, and luxury hospitality.

Her portfolio includes collaborations with Voltaire Light Design on the Arena di Verona, the Benetton Group Headquarters in Treviso, and Our Habitas AlUla; with In-visible lab on Hotel Aldrovandi in Rome and the Sheraton Spa in Como; and with Sergio Boccia Lighting Design on the JW Marriott in Jeju Island.

members.name: IDr. Vivian V. Gacad, PIID
bio: Vivian leads interior design, custom millwork, and turnkey fit-out execution as a partner specialist and Founder of Vivian Gacad Interior Design Services. Practicing since 2000 with a Bachelor of Arts in Interior Design from Assumption College (1997) and membership in the Philippine Institute of Interior Designers, she also owns and directs a furniture and modular cabinetry manufacturing facility employing craftsmen from Pampanga.

Her published portfolio has been featured in Real Living Magazine, Good Housekeeping, The Philippine Star, and Studio 23’s Welcome Home, alongside exhibition spaces for the Ayala Land Sonera “Living Space” Community Project and Samsung. She has directed hospitality, institutional, commercial, and luxury residential fit-outs including Bellaroca Island Resort in Marinduque, commercial holiday installations for six Ayala Malls branches, De La Salle Dasmariñas College of Engineering and Architecture, New Hatchin Grocerant, and private residences across Metro Manila.

members.name: Engr. Aldrin Fernandez
bio: Aldrin directs the studio’s control systems engineering and commissioning division, bringing over 12 years of experience in architectural lighting, façade illumination, electrical engineering, and intelligent controls. He governs system architecture, integration, and on-site commissioning across Lutron, Crestron, Philips Dynalite, DALI, DMX, iLight, and Interact Pro platforms.

His commissioned portfolio includes the Cebu–Cordova Link Expressway (CCLEX) Phase 2 façade, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, Hilton Manila, the Marriott Grand Ballroom, Shangri-La properties in Makati, EDSA, and Mactan, Conrad Hotel, Globe Telecom Headquarters, and St. Luke’s Medical Center.

members.name: Engr. Marry Grace Benigla, REE, SO2
bio: Grace prepares photometric calculations, electrical load schedules, and CAD layouts to ensure every studio deliverable passes local building code inspections. A Registered Electrical Engineer and certified Safety Officer, she graduated as an academic scholar and Dean’s Lister from Colegio de San Juan de Letran, earning Best Electrical Engineering Student and Best in Thesis.

She presented published research on solar-powered real-time monitoring systems at the 5th International Conference on Computer Applications Technology in Fukuoka, Japan, and completed training at the Parañaque Office of the Building Official reviewing electrical plans and load schedules.

meta.description: How CROIX Lighting Design Studio handles personal data submitted through project enquiries, email, and drawings.

hero.title: Privacy, plainly.
hero.intro: What we collect when you contact the studio, why we hold it, and how to ask us to correct or remove it.

privacy.content:
Who we are

CROIX Lighting Design Studio (“CROIX”, “we”, “us”) is a lighting design and engineering practice with an engineering hub in Parañaque City, Metro Manila, and a design practice in Milan through LUMEA Collective. This notice explains how we handle personal data in accordance with the Philippine Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173).

What we collect

When you contact the studio or engage us, we may collect:

  • Your name, firm, role, email address, and phone number.
  • Project information you choose to send, including location, sector, schedule, and notes.
  • Drawings, reflected ceiling plans, mood images, 3D views, and other files you email to us.
  • Correspondence, meeting notes, and documents created while preparing a proposal or delivering a project.

This website does not currently use advertising trackers. If analytics are added later, this notice will be updated before they are used.

Why we use it

  • To respond to your enquiry and prepare a fee proposal.
  • To deliver lighting design, photometric, controls, procurement, and commissioning services.
  • To coordinate with architects, contractors, suppliers, and consultants on your project.
  • To keep project records, issue invoices, and meet legal, tax, and professional obligations.

Legal basis

We rely on your consent when you submit an enquiry, on the steps needed to enter a contract with you, on our legitimate interest in running the studio, and on legal obligations where they apply.

Sharing

We do not sell personal data. We may share it with service providers who host our email or files, with consultants and collaborators working on your project, with professional advisers, and with authorities when the law requires it. These parties receive only what they need and are expected to keep it confidential.

Retention

We keep enquiry and project records for as long as needed to respond, deliver the work, and meet legal and professional requirements. Enquiries that do not proceed are reviewed periodically and deleted or anonymised when no longer needed.

Your rights

Subject to the Data Privacy Act, you may ask us to:

  • Confirm what personal data we hold about you and give you access to it.
  • Correct inaccurate or incomplete data.
  • Erase or block data that is no longer necessary, unlawfully held, or used for unauthorised purposes.
  • Object to processing, or withdraw consent where consent is the basis.
  • Complain to the National Privacy Commission.

To exercise a right, email info@croixlighting.com.ph. We may ask for enough information to confirm your identity before acting.

Security

We use reasonable organisational and technical measures to protect personal data. Email and file transfer are not completely secure, so please avoid sending sensitive personal information that is not needed for the project.

Changes

We may update this notice when our tools or processes change. The date at the top shows the latest revision.
